note: The simultaneous problem does not have a documented formal origin year. The component problems originate from: Arthur Wieferich (1909) posed the base-2 condition in 'Zum letzten Fermat'schen Theorem' (Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik, vol. 136, pp. 293-302); Dmitry Mirimanoff (1910) proved in 'Sur le dernier théorème de Fermat' (Comptes Rendus, vol. 150, pp. 204-206) that Wieferich primes automatically satisfy the base-3 condition. The question of whether a prime can satisfy BOTH conditions simultaneously appears to be an implicit modern research question arising from computational searches showing no such primes exist below 2^64, rather than an explicitly stated historical conjecture.
